entries.name: Kinesis
entries.description: AWS's family of real-time data streaming tools:

children.name: Data Streams / Analytics
children.description: Collects and processes data as it arrives, in real time (like a live pipe of data).

children.name: Data Firehose
children.description: Automatically loads streaming data into S3, Redshift, etc. Simpler than Data Streams.

children.name: Client Library (KCL)
children.description: A library used to build your own app that reads and processes records from a Kinesis data stream.

children.name: Producer Library (KPL)
children.description: A client library apps use to efficiently batch and send records into a Kinesis data stream.

entries.name: Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka)
entries.description: A managed way to run Apache Kafka for ingesting and processing real-time streaming data.

entries.name: Athena
entries.description: Run SQL queries directly on files sitting in S3. No database needed.

children.name: Federated Query
children.description: Lets Athena also run SQL against other data sources (like a live DynamoDB table) through a connector, without first copying that data into S3.

entries.name: QuickSight
entries.description: Build dashboards and charts (BI tool) from your data.

children.name: SPICE
children.description: QuickSight's built-in in-memory engine; load data into it so dashboards query fast without hitting the original data source every time.

entries.name: Redshift
entries.description: A data warehouse. Built for big, heavy analytics queries.

children.name: Data API
children.description: Lets apps run SQL queries against Redshift over a simple API call instead of managing a persistent database connection.

children.name: Spectrum
children.description: Lets Redshift run SQL queries directly against data sitting in S3, without loading it into the cluster first.

entries.name: Glue
entries.description: Finds, cleans, and moves data between sources (ETL = Extract, Transform, Load). Has "crawlers" that scan data and "job bookmarks" that remember what's already processed.

children.name: Glue Studio
children.description: A visual, drag-and-drop interface for building and monitoring Glue ETL jobs (no need to hand-write scripts).

children.name: ML Transforms
children.description: A Glue feature that uses machine learning during ETL, e.g. matching/deduplicating similar records — not a general ML model-building platform.

children.name: Elastic Views
children.description: (Discontinued) Used to build a materialized view combining data from a database into S3 and kept it auto-synced.

entries.name: Lake Formation
entries.description: Helps you build a "data lake" (a big organized S3 storage area) quickly and securely.

children.name: Blueprints
children.description: A pre-built Lake Formation template that automates ingesting data (e.g., from a database) into an S3 data lake.

children.name: Tag-Based Access Control (LF-TBAC)
children.description: Grants data lake access by tagging databases/tables/columns instead of managing permissions resource-by-resource — scales much better for cross-account sharing.

entries.name: OpenSearch Service
entries.description: Search and log analytics engine (used for searching large text/log data, not for BI dashboards).

entries.name: Amazon EMR
entries.description: A managed big-data cluster service (runs tools like Hadoop/Spark/Hive) for processing huge datasets — heavier and more manual than Glue.

entries.name: CloudWatch Logs Insights
entries.description: Lets you interactively search and analyze log data in CloudWatch Logs using a query language.

entries.name: Amazon DynamoDB
entries.description: A fully managed, serverless NoSQL key-value/document database with single-digit-millisecond performance at any scale. Beyond the basics, DynamoDB has several add-on capabilities:

children.name: Accelerator (DAX)
children.description: An in-memory cache that sits in front of DynamoDB to speed up read performance (does not help with writes).

children.name: Streams
children.description: A time-ordered log of item-level changes in a table; can trigger a Lambda function whenever data changes.

children.name: Global Tables
children.description: Automatically replicates a DynamoDB table across multiple AWS regions for multi-region reads/writes and resilience.

children.name: Time to Live (TTL)
children.description: Automatically deletes items from a table after a timestamp you set expires — free, no extra code needed.

children.name: Transactions
children.description: Groups multiple item writes into one all-or-nothing atomic operation.

children.name: Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)
children.description: Continuous, native backup of a table (can export to S3) that lets you restore to any point in time, without using up the table's read/write capacity.

children.name: Standard-IA Table Class
children.description: A cheaper-to-store table class for infrequently accessed data (trades lower storage cost for higher per-request cost) — the DynamoDB equivalent of S3 Standard-IA.

children.name: Read/Write Capacity Units (RCU/WCU)
children.description: In provisioned-capacity mode, you set a fixed number of Read Capacity Units and Write Capacity Units per second the table can handle; exceeding them throttles requests unless you switch to on-demand mode instead.

entries.name: Amazon RDS
entries.description: A managed relational database service (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server) that handles patching, backups, and failover for you. Beyond the basics, RDS has several add-on capabilities:

children.name: Proxy
children.description: Sits between your app and an RDS/Aurora database, pooling connections so many short-lived Lambda calls don't exhaust the database's connection limit.

children.name: Custom
children.description: A managed RDS option that still lets you log in and customize the underlying OS/database, unlike standard RDS.

children.name: Performance Insights
children.description: A built-in dashboard that visualizes database load so you can spot performance problems.

children.name: Query Editor
children.description: A browser-based SQL editor in the RDS console for querying Aurora Serverless (via the Data API) without installing a separate database client — only works on RDS/Aurora, not on files in S3.

entries.name: Aurora
entries.description: AWS's own MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database engine, built for the cloud to be faster and more fault-tolerant than standard RDS engines at similar cost. Beyond the standard managed relational database:

children.name: Global Database
children.description: Replicates an Aurora database across AWS regions with very low lag — good for cross-region disaster recovery.

children.name: Serverless
children.description: An on-demand version of Aurora that automatically scales database capacity up and down based on load.

children.name: Auto Scaling
children.description: Automatically adds/removes Aurora read replicas as read traffic changes.

entries.name: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
entries.description: A managed document database that "speaks" MongoDB's API, so a MongoDB-based app can run on AWS with no code changes.

entries.name: Amazon ElastiCache
entries.description: A managed in-memory data store/cache (Redis or Memcached) that sits in front of a database to serve very low-latency reads and reduce load on the primary data store.

entries.name: Amazon SageMaker Pipelines
entries.description: Builds and automates end-to-end machine learning workflows (e.g., can auto-run when new data files arrive).

entries.name: Amazon AppFlow
entries.description: A managed integration service with built-in SaaS connectors (e.g., Salesforce) that securely moves data into AWS services like S3, encrypting data in transit and supporting a customer-managed KMS key at rest.

entries.name: AWS Data Exchange
entries.description: Find, subscribe to, or privately publish third-party data sets/data products to other AWS accounts.

entries.name: Secrets Manager
entries.description: Safely stores passwords/API keys and can auto-rotate them.

entries.name: Systems Manager Parameter Store
entries.description: Also stores config values/secrets, but simpler (no auto-rotation).

entries.name: Cognito
entries.description: Handles user sign-up/login (User Pool) and gives logged-in users temporary AWS access (Identity Pool).

entries.name: Firewall Manager
entries.description: Lets you set one security rule and apply it across many AWS accounts at once.

entries.name: Shield / Shield Advanced
entries.description: Protects your app from DDoS (flood) attacks.

entries.name: Network Firewall
entries.description: A firewall inside your VPC that inspects and filters network traffic.

entries.name: GuardDuty
entries.description: Watches your account for suspicious/malicious activity (like a security camera).

entries.name: Inspector
entries.description: Scans EC2/containers/Lambda for known software vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Macie
entries.description: Scans S3 for sensitive data (like credit card numbers) using AI.

entries.name: Amazon Detective
entries.description: Analyzes and visualizes log data (VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, GuardDuty findings) to help investigate the root cause of a security finding after it's raised.

entries.name: AWS Audit Manager
entries.description: Continuously collects evidence and maps it to a chosen compliance framework (e.g., PCI DSS) to simplify audit prep.

entries.name: AWS Organizations / SCP (Service Control Policy)
entries.description: Manage many AWS accounts together; SCPs are rules that block actions across all of them.

entries.name: Control Tower
entries.description: Sets up and governs a multi-account AWS environment with built-in guardrails.

entries.name: ACM (Certificate Manager)
entries.description: Creates and manages SSL/TLS certificates (for HTTPS).

entries.name: AWS Config
entries.description: Tracks and reports if your AWS resources follow the rules you set (detects problems, doesn't block them).

entries.name: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
entries.description: Lets you open a secure shell on an EC2 instance from the console/CLI — no open SSH ports, no key pairs, no bastion host, just an attached IAM role.

entries.name: STS (Security Token Service) / AssumeRole
entries.description: Issues short-lived, temporary credentials so a role in one AWS account can securely access resources in another account, instead of using long-term keys.

entries.name: IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA)
entries.description: An EKS feature that lets each Kubernetes pod assume its own narrow IAM role, instead of every pod sharing the node's permissions.

entries.name: IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO)
entries.description: Lets users sign in once to access many AWS accounts/apps, using permission sets tied to directory groups.

entries.name: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall)
entries.description: Filters and blocks malicious HTTP(S) requests (SQL injection, XSS, rate-based abuse) before they reach CloudFront, an ALB, or API Gateway, using rules you define.

entries.name: AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management)
entries.description: Controls who (users, groups, roles) can do what (permissions via policies) across your AWS account; the foundation of AWS access control. Beyond basic users/groups/roles/policies:

children.name: Account Password Policy
children.description: One account-wide setting that enforces password complexity and rotation rules for every IAM user, including future ones.

children.name: aws:PrincipalOrgID / aws:PrincipalOrgPaths
children.description: Policy condition keys you add to a resource policy (e.g., an S3 bucket policy) so it auto-grants access to every current and future account in your AWS Organization, without listing each account.

entries.name: AWS Directory Service
entries.description: AWS's family of managed directory options for Windows/Active Directory-based authentication, including Simple AD, AWS Managed Microsoft AD, and AD Connector.

children.name: AWS Managed Microsoft AD
children.description: A real Microsoft Active Directory that AWS runs for you; can trust an existing on-premises AD.

children.name: AD Connector
children.description: A lightweight proxy that redirects sign-in requests to your existing on-premises Active Directory, without copying user data into AWS.

entries.name: AWS KMS (Key Management Service)
entries.description: Creates and controls the encryption keys used to encrypt data across AWS services; keys are used for encrypt/decrypt operations but the key material never leaves KMS unencrypted.

children.name: Multi-Region Keys
children.description: A KMS key whose key material is replicated into multiple regions, so data encrypted in one region can be decrypted with the matching key in another.

entries.name: AWS Client VPN
entries.description: A managed VPN service that gives individual remote employees a secure encrypted connection into AWS/on-prem networks from their own laptop.

entries.name: AWS Account Alternate Contacts
entries.description: Lets you add extra contacts (besides the root user) so important account notifications reliably reach someone.

entries.name: Amazon S3 Pre-Signed URLs
entries.description: A time-limited link that grants temporary access to one private S3 object (upload or download) without changing bucket permissions.

entries.name: Amazon CloudFront
entries.description: AWS's content delivery network (CDN): caches and serves content from edge locations close to users to speed up delivery of both static and dynamic content worldwide.

entries.name: CloudFront (access control)
entries.description: Ways to restrict who can reach private CloudFront content:

children.name: Origin Access Identity (OAI)
children.description: A special identity attached to a CloudFront distribution and granted exclusive S3 access, so content can only be fetched through CloudFront, never directly from S3.

children.name: Signed URLs / Signed Cookies
children.description: Signed URLs embed the auth info in the link itself (for clients without cookie support); signed cookies keep the original URL unchanged and grant access via a cookie.

children.name: Field-Level Encryption
children.description: Encrypts specific sensitive form fields right at the CloudFront edge with a public key, so only backend systems with the matching private key can decrypt them — protects the data even after HTTPS ends.

entries.name: API Gateway (access control)
entries.description: Ways to gate who can call an API:

children.name: Usage Plans & API Keys
children.description: Issue API keys to known clients and set throttling/quota limits per key — a simple way to gate access (e.g., only paying subscribers).

children.name: Resource Policy
children.description: A policy attached to an API that allows/denies requests based on conditions like the caller's source IP address.

entries.name: SQS-Managed Server-Side Encryption (SSE-SQS)
entries.description: A built-in SQS encryption option using keys SQS manages itself — no KMS setup or decrypt permissions needed (simpler, less control than SSE-KMS).

entries.name: RDS IAM Database Authentication
entries.description: Lets apps connect to an RDS database using temporary IAM-generated tokens instead of a traditional username/password.

entries.name: AWS CloudTrail
entries.description: Logs every API call/action taken in your AWS account (who did what, when, from where) for auditing, troubleshooting, and compliance.

children.name: Data Events
children.description: An optional, more detailed logging level that records object-level activity (e.g., individual S3 object reads/writes) — off by default, unlike basic management-event logging.

entries.name: Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud)
entries.description: Your own logically isolated, private network within AWS where you launch resources and control subnets, routing, and IP addressing.

children.name: Security Group
children.description: A stateful, instance-level virtual firewall — allow rules only; return traffic is automatically permitted.

children.name: Network ACL
children.description: A stateless, subnet-level firewall with explicit allow AND deny rules, evaluated in order — a second layer of defense behind security groups.

children.name: Elastic IP
children.description: A static public IPv4 address you allocate to your account and can attach to (or move between) EC2 instances/network interfaces.

children.name: Internet Gateway
children.description: Attached to a VPC to let resources in public subnets send and receive traffic directly to and from the internet.

entries.name: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
entries.description: Automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets (EC2 instances, containers, IPs). An Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS, path/host-based routing); a Network Load Balancer (NLB) operates at Layer 4 for extreme performance and static IPs; the legacy Classic Load Balancer (CLB) is largely superseded by the two.

entries.name: Global Accelerator
entries.description: Routes users to the nearest AWS entry point using AWS's private network. Good for gaming, APIs, non-web traffic.

entries.name: VPC Endpoint / PrivateLink
entries.description: Lets your private network talk to AWS services (or another company's service) without going over the public internet.

entries.name: VPC Peering
entries.description: A direct private connection between two VPCs (even across accounts/regions) so they can talk using private IPs, as if on the same network.

entries.name: NAT Gateway
entries.description: Lets private-subnet resources reach the internet (outbound only), fully managed by AWS.

entries.name: NAT Instance
entries.description: The older, self-managed (you patch/scale it yourself) EC2-based alternative to a NAT Gateway.

entries.name: Egress-Only Internet Gateway
entries.description: Gives IPv6 resources in a subnet outbound-only internet access, blocking anything initiated from the internet.

entries.name: Virtual Private Gateway (VGW)
entries.description: The AWS-side endpoint that terminates a VPN or Direct Connect connection and routes traffic between a VPC and your on-premises network.

entries.name: Direct Connect
entries.description: A dedicated private network line from your office/data center straight to AWS.

children.name: Direct Connect Gateway
children.description: Lets one Direct Connect connection reach multiple VPCs, including ones in different AWS Regions.

children.name: Virtual Interface (VIF)
children.description: The logical connection carried over a Direct Connect link: a private VIF reaches resources inside a VPC, while a public VIF reaches public AWS service endpoints (like S3) over the dedicated line instead of the internet.

entries.name: Site-to-Site VPN
entries.description: An encrypted tunnel connecting your network to AWS over the internet.

entries.name: EventBridge
entries.description: Routes "events" (things that happened) between AWS services automatically.

entries.name: Amazon Route 53
entries.description: AWS's highly available managed DNS service; also supports domain registration and health-check-based failover.

children.name: Advanced Routing Policies
children.description: Beyond basic DNS, Route 53 can route by geographic location (geolocation), lowest latency, traffic percentage (weighted), or return several healthy answers at once for clients to pick randomly (multivalue answer).

entries.name: Amazon API Gateway
entries.description: A fully managed service to create, publish, secure, and monitor REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at any scale, typically fronting Lambda or other backends.

entries.name: API Gateway (private connectivity)
entries.description: Ways to keep an API off the public internet:

children.name: VPC Link
children.description: Lets a public REST API in API Gateway securely reach backend resources (like containers) sitting in private VPC subnets, without exposing them to the internet.

children.name: Private Integration
children.description: The general term for connecting an API privately into a VPC instead of over the public internet.

entries.name: AWS Transit Gateway
entries.description: A central regional network hub that lets hundreds of VPCs (and on-premises networks, via Direct Connect/VPN) all connect through one managed gateway instead of a full mesh of individual peering connections; Transit Gateway peering links hubs together across regions.

entries.name: Transit VPC
entries.description: An older, self-managed hub-and-spoke pattern that routes traffic between VPCs/on-premises through a central VPC running your own router software — mostly superseded by Transit Gateway.

entries.name: AWS App Mesh
entries.description: A service mesh giving microservices (e.g., on ECS) application-level networking — communicate, monitor, and control traffic between services.

entries.name: CloudFront (traffic & response config)
entries.description: Non-caching configuration options for a distribution:

children.name: Origin Request Policy
children.description: Controls which headers/cookies/query strings CloudFront forwards to the origin on a cache miss — configuration only, cannot resize images or run processing logic.

children.name: Response Headers Policy
children.description: Adds or modifies HTTP headers on responses sent back to viewers — also configuration only, no content transformation.

children.name: Geographic Restrictions (Geo-Blocking)
children.description: Uses a country allow-list or block-list to permit/deny viewers by geographic location.

entries.name: Application Migration Service (MGN)
entries.description: Copies ("lift and shift") your on-premises servers into AWS as EC2 instances.

entries.name: Database Migration Service (DMS)
entries.description: Moves databases into AWS, and can keep syncing while the old one is still running.

entries.name: Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)
entries.description: Converts a database's structure from one engine to another (e.g., Oracle → PostgreSQL).

entries.name: App2Container (A2C)
entries.description: Automatically packages an existing app into a Docker container.

entries.name: AWS DataSync
entries.description: Uses an on-premises agent to automatically move large amounts of data (e.g., an on-prem NFS share) into AWS storage like S3 or EFS, without manual copying.

entries.name: AWS Snowcone
entries.description: A small, lightweight, portable version of Snowball Edge for locations with limited space/bandwidth.

entries.name: AWS Transfer Family
entries.description: A fully managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP server backed by S3, so external partners can upload files straight into your S3 data lake with no server to manage.

entries.name: AWS Snowmobile
entries.description: An actual shipping-container truck AWS sends you to physically move exabyte-scale data — for transfers far too big even for a Snowball Edge.

entries.name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS)
entries.description: Continuously replicates disk-level changes from an on-premises (or other) server to AWS so it can be quickly recovered after an outage — whole-server block replication, not database-aware.

entries.name: ECS (Elastic Container Service)
entries.description: Runs and manages Docker containers.

entries.name: Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry)
entries.description: A managed Docker container image registry: push, store, scan, and pull the images your ECS/EKS/Fargate tasks run.

entries.name: EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service)
entries.description: AWS's managed Kubernetes service — runs a standard Kubernetes cluster without you managing the control plane.

children.name: Managed Node Groups
children.description: Lets EKS automatically provision, scale, and update the underlying EC2 (including Spot) worker nodes for you.

entries.name: Fargate
entries.description: Runs containers without you managing any servers (serverless containers); works with both ECS and EKS.

entries.name: AWS Load Balancer Controller
entries.description: Automatically provisions and configures AWS load balancers to route traffic to containers running on EKS/EC2.

entries.name: AWS App Runner
entries.description: Fully managed hosting for containerized web apps/APIs — quick to deploy, but only for HTTP-facing apps, not batch jobs.

entries.name: AWS ParallelCluster
entries.description: An open-source tool for deploying and managing High Performance Computing (HPC) clusters on AWS.

entries.name: Amazon Lightsail
entries.description: A simplified, cheaper "starter" VPS that bundles compute+storage+networking, for simple apps that don't need full EC2.

entries.name: Amazon MQ
entries.description: A managed message broker (like RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ) — an alternative to SQS/SNS when you need those specific protocols.

entries.name: AWS Batch
entries.description: Runs large batch jobs and automatically manages the compute needed.

entries.name: AWS Application Auto Scaling
entries.description: Automatically adjusts capacity for resources like ECS services (not just EC2) using target-tracking policies.

entries.name: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
entries.description: Automatically launches or terminates EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to match demand and keep a healthy instance count, based on scaling policies (target tracking, step, or scheduled).

entries.name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
entries.description: A platform-as-a-service (PaaS): upload your application code and Beanstalk automatically handles provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and deployment on your behalf.

entries.name: AWS Step Functions
entries.description: Coordinates multiple Lambda functions and other AWS services into a visual, reliable multi-step workflow (state machine), handling retries and error branching for you.

entries.name: Amazon EC2
entries.description: Resizable virtual servers ("instances") in the cloud, billed by the instance type/size and purchasing option you choose. Beyond the standard instance:

children.name: Amazon Machine Image (AMI)
children.description: The template (OS + software + config) used to launch an EC2 instance; you can use an AWS-provided AMI, one from the Marketplace, or build your own.

children.name: Placement Groups (Cluster / Partition)
children.description: Controls how EC2 instances are physically placed on hardware; a cluster placement group packs them close together in one AZ for the lowest latency/highest throughput.

children.name: Serial Console
children.description: A direct, out-of-band terminal into an EC2 instance — a troubleshooting tool, not for routine remote admin.

children.name: Instance Store
children.description: Temporary block storage physically attached to the host — very fast, but wiped when the instance stops/terminates.

entries.name: AWS Lambda
entries.description: Runs your code in response to triggers without you provisioning or managing any servers; you're billed only for the compute time you actually use. Beyond a basic function:

children.name: Lambda@Edge
children.description: Runs Lambda functions at CloudFront's edge locations, to process/filter requests close to users.

children.name: Provisioned Concurrency
children.description: Keeps a set number of Lambda environments "pre-warmed" so there's no cold-start delay.

children.name: Reserved Concurrency
children.description: Caps/guarantees a fixed amount of concurrent Lambda executions, but does not pre-warm anything (cold starts can still happen).

entries.name: Spot / Reserved / Scheduled Reserved Instances / Savings Plans
entries.description: Ways to pay less for EC2: Spot = cheap but can be interrupted; Reserved = commit 1-3 years for a discount; Scheduled Reserved = reserved capacity only for a recurring time window; Savings Plans = commit to a $/hour spend across EC2/Fargate/Lambda for a discount.

entries.name: Amazon EBS (Elastic Block Store)
entries.description: Persistent, redundant block storage volumes that attach to a single EC2 instance, like a virtual hard drive; volume types (gp3, io2, etc.) trade off cost, throughput, and provisioned IOPS.

children.name: Multi-Attach
children.description: Lets a single Provisioned IOPS (io1/io2) EBS volume be attached to multiple EC2 instances at once in the same AZ, for clustered applications that manage concurrent writes themselves.

entries.name: Amazon EFS (Elastic File System)
entries.description: A managed, elastic NFS file system that many EC2 instances (or Lambda functions) can mount and share concurrently across Availability Zones.

entries.name: FSx
entries.description: AWS's family of managed, high-performance shared file systems:

children.name: for Lustre
children.description: Built for supercomputing/HPC workloads.

children.name: for Windows File Server
children.description: Native Windows SMB shares, single- or multi-AZ.

children.name: for NetApp ONTAP
children.description: Runs NetApp's ONTAP file system, with configurable data-tiering for high-throughput, low-latency multi-instance access.

children.name: for OpenZFS
children.description: Built on the OpenZFS file system; unlike the other FSx types, only supports single-AZ deployments.

children.name: File Gateway
children.description: A Storage Gateway type giving on-premises servers cached, low-latency local access to a fully managed FSx for Windows File Server share running in AWS.

entries.name: Storage Gateway
entries.description: AWS's family of hybrid on-premises-to-cloud storage appliances:

children.name: File Gateway
children.description: A virtual device that connects your on-premises servers to S3 as a file share, with local caching for speed.

children.name: Volume Gateway
children.description: Presents cloud-backed block storage volumes to on-prem apps over iSCSI (cached volumes = hot data local + full data in S3; stored volumes = full data on-prem, backed up to S3).

children.name: Tape Gateway
children.description: Presents a virtual tape library so on-prem backup software can archive to S3/Glacier as if writing to physical tapes.

entries.name: Amazon S3
entries.description: Durable, virtually unlimited object storage accessed over HTTP(S) — the default place to park files, backups, static assets, and data-lake data. Beyond the basics, S3 has many add-on capabilities:

children.name: Transfer Acceleration
children.description: Speeds up uploads to S3 from far-away locations.

children.name: Multipart Upload
children.description: Splits a large file into smaller parts uploaded independently (then reassembled) — used for large object transfers over HTTPS.

children.name: Lifecycle Policy
children.description: A rule that automatically moves old files to cheaper storage over time.

children.name: Glacier / Glacier Deep Archive
children.description: Very cheap, slow-to-retrieve storage for long-term archives.

children.name: Glacier Select
children.description: Lets you run SQL-like queries directly against data inside a Glacier archive, without retrieving/decompressing the whole archive first.

children.name: Intelligent-Tiering
children.description: Automatically moves files between storage tiers based on how often they're used (has a small per-object monitoring fee).

children.name: One Zone-IA
children.description: Cheaper storage that lives in only one data center (less durable, less available).

children.name: Object Lock
children.description: Makes objects immutable (write-once-read-many) with either a fixed retention period or a legal hold, so they can't be changed or deleted until released.

children.name: Bucket Keys
children.description: A short-lived, bucket-level key derived from a KMS key that S3 reuses for many objects, cutting KMS API calls (and cost) while still using SSE-KMS.

children.name: Cross-Region Replication (CRR) / Replication
children.description: Automatically and asynchronously copies new objects from one bucket to another (same or different region).

children.name: Inventory
children.description: A scheduled report listing all objects in a bucket plus metadata (like encryption status) — handy for auditing millions of files without listing them by hand.

children.name: Batch Operations
children.description: Runs one managed job (e.g., copy, re-encrypt) across millions of existing objects at once.

children.name: Event Notifications
children.description: Automatically triggers an action (e.g., invoking Lambda) whenever an object is created, modified, or deleted.

children.name: Server Access Logging
children.description: Records detailed logs of every request made to a bucket — good for auditing, not for live change-detection.

children.name: Static Website Hosting
children.description: Serves static content (HTML/CSS/JS) directly from a bucket as a website.

children.name: MFA Delete
children.description: Requires a second authentication factor to permanently delete an object version — protects versioned files from accidental/malicious deletion.

children.name: Object Lambda
children.description: Attaches a Lambda function to S3 GET requests so data (e.g., PII) can be transformed/redacted on the fly per requesting app, without keeping separate duplicate copies.

children.name: Block Public Access
children.description: A bucket- or account-level setting that force-keeps objects private, overriding any bucket policy or ACL that would otherwise expose them.

children.name: Storage Lens
children.description: An organization-wide analytics dashboard showing detailed S3 usage/activity metrics (request counts, retrieval rates) — good for spotting unused or rarely-accessed buckets.

children.name: Reduced Redundancy Storage (RRS)
children.description: A legacy, lower-durability, lower-cost storage class — deprecated, not recommended for new workloads.

children.name: Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3 / SSE-C / SSE-KMS)
children.description: Encrypts objects at rest: SSE-S3 uses keys S3 manages itself (simplest, no setup); SSE-KMS uses a KMS key you control, giving audit logging and rotation; SSE-C lets you supply your own encryption key with every request, and S3 never stores it.

entries.name: AWS Backup
entries.description: A centralized backup service: define a schedule and retention period (e.g., daily, kept 2 years) and apply it across resources like RDS/Aurora/EBS.

children.name: Vault Lock
children.description: Locks a backup vault into a true immutable, write-once-read-many state; in compliance mode, not even the root user can alter or delete backups before the retention period ends.

entries.name: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM)
entries.description: Automates creating, retaining, and deleting EBS snapshots on a schedule.

entries.name: Snowball Edge
entries.description: A physical device AWS ships you to move huge amounts of data when internet transfer is too slow.

entries.name: Amazon RDS Storage Auto Scaling
entries.description: Automatically grows a database's allocated storage online, with no downtime, once free space drops below a threshold.

entries.name: Amazon Transcribe
entries.description: Automatically converts speech in audio recordings (in many languages) into written text.

entries.name: Amazon Translate
entries.description: Automatically translates text from one language into another.

entries.name: Amazon Comprehend
entries.description: Natural-language processing service that reads text and detects things like sentiment (positive/negative).

entries.name: Amazon Polly
entries.description: Converts written text into lifelike speech (the opposite of Transcribe).

entries.name: Amazon Lex
entries.description: Builds voice/text conversational chatbots (not for sentiment analysis or reports).

entries.name: Amazon Rekognition
entries.description: Analyzes images and video (not text) — e.g., detecting objects or faces.

entries.name: Amazon Textract
entries.description: Extracts text and data from scanned documents (OCR) — different from transcribing audio (Transcribe) or translating languages (Translate).

entries.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
entries.description: Automatically inspects your account and gives recommendations across cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits.

entries.name: Amazon CloudWatch
entries.description: Collects metrics, logs, and events from your AWS resources and lets you build dashboards and alarms to monitor and react to them. Beyond basic alarms/metrics/dashboards:

children.name: Synthetics
children.description: Scripted "canaries" that periodically test your app's endpoints to proactively catch availability/performance problems.

children.name: Composite Alarms
children.description: Combines multiple existing alarms with AND/OR logic so a notification only fires when several conditions happen together (fewer false alerts).

children.name: Metric Streams
children.description: Continuously streams CloudWatch metrics in near real time to a destination like Kinesis Data Firehose, without polling.

children.name: Logs (export / subscription filter)
children.description: Export logs to S3 for long-term storage, or stream them live to another service (like OpenSearch) via a subscription filter.

children.name: Agent
children.description: Optional software you install on EC2 instances to collect extra metrics (like memory utilization) or custom app metrics that CloudWatch doesn't gather by default.

children.name: Container Insights
children.description: Collects and summarizes performance metrics/logs specifically from containerized apps — a monitoring tool, not an event trigger.

entries.name: AWS Systems Manager
entries.description: A management hub for operating your EC2 and hybrid on-premises infrastructure at scale (patching, running commands, storing config) — includes Session Manager and Parameter Store. Beyond Session Manager and Parameter Store:

children.name: Automation
children.description: Runs pre-built or custom "documents" that script multi-step operational tasks (e.g., patching an instance and re-registering it with a load balancer).

children.name: Maintenance Windows
children.description: Defines a recurring scheduled time window during which tasks like patching are allowed to run.

children.name: State Manager
children.description: Continuously applies and enforces a configuration you define across your managed instances.

children.name: Run Command
children.description: Remotely runs a command/script on managed EC2 instances without logging into them individually.

children.name: Inventory
children.description: Automatically collects metadata (OS version, patch status, installed software) from managed EC2 instances.

entries.name: AWS Budgets
entries.description: Set a spending/usage threshold and get automatically alerted when you're forecast to cross it.

children.name: Budgets Actions
children.description: Can automatically apply a restrictive IAM policy or SCP once a spending threshold is hit, instead of just sending an alert.

entries.name: AWS Cost Explorer
entries.description: Visualize, filter, and report on your AWS spending (e.g., by user or tag) — no threshold-alerting built in.

entries.name: AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR)
entries.description: A detailed, granular export of billing data you can query with tools like Athena.

entries.name: AWS Cost Allocation Tags
entries.description: User-defined or AWS-defined tags (e.g., "department") that must be activated from the management account's billing console before Cost Explorer can group/report spending by that tag org-wide.

entries.name: AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor
entries.description: A console tool to quickly find and report on resources across services/regions based on their tags.

entries.name: AWS X-Ray
entries.description: Traces and visualizes how individual requests flow through and perform across a distributed application's components — not an infrastructure inventory tool.

entries.name: Workload Discovery on AWS
entries.description: Automatically builds visual architecture diagrams of your AWS resources and how they relate, by pulling from AWS Config and CloudTrail across accounts/regions.

entries.name: AWS Reserved Instance Marketplace
entries.description: Lets you sell your unused, unexpired EC2 Reserved Instances to other AWS customers (Savings Plans have no equivalent resale option).

entries.name: AWS CloudFormation
entries.description: Infrastructure as code: define your AWS resources in a template (JSON/YAML) and CloudFormation creates, updates, or deletes them together as one managed stack.

entries.name: AWS Amplify
entries.description: A managed platform for building, hosting, and deploying full-stack web/mobile apps with built-in CI/CD.

entries.name: AWS AppSync
entries.description: A managed service for building and running GraphQL APIs.

entries.name: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)
entries.description: A managed service for sending (and receiving) email programmatically, e.g., for automated notifications.

entries.name: Amazon WorkMail
entries.description: A managed business email and calendar service.

entries.name: Amazon Pinpoint
entries.description: A managed service for sending targeted, personalized messages to users across email, SMS, push notifications, and voice.

entries.name: Amazon Connect
entries.description: A cloud-based contact center service for setting up customer service call/chat centers without on-premises hardware.

entries.name: Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service)
entries.description: A managed pub/sub messaging service: publish a message once to a topic and fan it out to many subscribers (SQS queues, Lambda, email, SMS, HTTP endpoints) at once.

children.name: Message Filtering
children.description: Lets each subscriber (e.g., an SQS queue) receive only a subset of messages published to a topic, based on filter rules — used to fan out and route messages by type.

entries.name: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service)
entries.description: A managed message queue that decouples producers and consumers; supports Standard queues (high throughput, at-least-once, best-effort ordering) and FIFO queues (strict ordering, exactly-once processing).

children.name: Extended Client Library
children.description: A Java library that auto-stores SQS message payloads bigger than 256 KB in S3 and sends only a small pointer through the queue — minimal code change to handle much larger messages.

entries.name: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)
entries.description: Securely shares AWS resources across multiple AWS accounts — not a tool for detecting or fixing publicly exposed S3 buckets.

entries.name: AWS Service Catalog
entries.description: Lets admins publish a catalog of pre-approved, standardized resource configurations so staff can only deploy already-sanctioned setups.

entries.name: AWS Marketplace
entries.description: A digital catalog to find, buy, and deploy pre-configured third-party software and AMIs on AWS.
